issues.what: Reported by p2020-p2029: the Jan-1 2020 anchor shows the Free Zone as Moroccan and Dakhla reversed (Moroccan land occupied by the SADR). Root cause as the report says: the gazetteer's 'W. Sahara' is only the Free Zone, so morocco/ledger/25 and the SADR 1976 found reach only it. Now settled where it happens: the republic owns the territory by its claim from February 1976 (events/11), the Free Zone is contested until the ceasefire (events/12, ledger/8 closes it in September 1991), Morocco occupies the part west of the berm. Trial: the end-2019 anchor has the Free Zone 331/331 direct republic and Saguia + Río de Oro (644 cells, Dakhla included) republic land occupied by Morocco.

Orchestrator item, Morocco's 1976 share: morocco/ledger/23-25 name only the gazetteer's 'Western Sahara'; with francoist-spain/ledger/10 handing all 975 cells to Morocco, the window agent's events/4 (SADR gain from Spain) moved nothing and the 47 Oued ed-Dahab cells north of the Tiris (north of 24 N) were never marked Moroccan. Events/5 (Laayoune-Boujdour unit and the Smara part, 'Morocco took over the Saguia El Hamra and the northern two-thirds') is kept; events/13 adds the 47 cells. After the patch all 418 cells of Saguia and Río de Oro north of 24 N west of the berm are the republic's, occupied by Morocco, from 1976.
issues.patch: p1970-p1979.json: events/13 (events/11 is the republic's ownership of the territory; events/4 and events/5 stay as the window agent wrote them)

issues.what: Orchestrator item, Mauritania's Tiris al-Gharbiyya 1976-1979: mauritania/ledger/2 takes the Tiris from francoist-spain, which ended in November 1975, so it took nothing and the Mauritanian share was never drawn (mauritania_1976 snap 'kept by others 195'). Now Mauritania gains the Tiris (401 cells) from the republic in April 1976 and holds it contested by the republic until the peace treaty. Trial: end 1976-1978 all 401 Tiris cells are Mauritanian land contested by the republic; the snap's 'kept by others' falls from 195 to 20.

Orchestrator item, Morocco's take-over of the Tiris in August 1979: mauritania/ledger/3 gives the 401 cells to Morocco as Moroccan land (the republic's ledger/7 then read as the republic occupying Moroccan land, 226 cells, and 175 cells east of the berm Moroccan outright until 1991). Now the republic regains the Tiris by its claim (events/16), Morocco occupies the 226 cells west of the berm (events/17), and the 175 cells east of the berm are the republic's land contested by Morocco until the 1991 ceasefire (events/18). Trial: end 1979-1990 as described, from September 1991 the 175 east cells are direct republic.

Orchestrator item, the berm years (1980-1991): with the entries above the map for 1980-1990 is the republic's territory with the Free Zone contested by Morocco and the west of the berm occupied by Morocco; the republic's ledger/8 closes the contest in September 1991 (verified: end 1990 contested 331, end 1991 direct 331) and the occupation continues. The berm page dates six walls (August 1980-June 1982 the useful triangle; Amgala December 1983-January 1984; Jdiriya and Haouza April-May 1984; Mahbes and Farciya December 1984-January 1985; Guelta Zemmur, Bir Anzarane and Dakhla May-September 1985; Auserd, Tichla and Bir Ganduz February-April 1987) but names places, not areas, so the year-by-year spread of Moroccan control is not drawn: the final berm line (the gazetteer's 'W. Sahara' boundary) is used from 1976, the republic's land being drawn occupied west of it.

End of 1975: francoist-spain/ledger/10 (dossier, handed the whole territory to Morocco on 14 November 1975) makes all 975 cells Moroccan at the end of 1975, while the Western Sahara War page says Spain 'ceded the administrative control of the territory to Mauritania and Morocco on 14 November 1975' and the partition is dated April 1976 (Western Sahara page); mauritania/ledger/1 has Mauritanian troops in Tichla and La Guera on 20 December 1975. Not touched: the pages give no area for a December 1975 Mauritanian holding, and the 1976 entries redraw the partition from February.
